artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be an arbitrary matrix and let $b\in\mathbb{C}^n$ be a random starting vector (e.g., with i.i.d. complex Gaussian entries). For an integer $1\le k\le n$, let $\mathcal{K}_k(A,b)=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,A^2b,\ldots,A^{k-1}b\}$ denote the associated Krylov subspace, and let $Q\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times k}$ be a matrix whose columns form an orthonormal basis of $\mathcal{K}_k(A,b)$. Set $H=Q^*AQ\in\mathbb{C}^{k\times k}$ (the Krylov compression of $A$).

Recall that, for a diagonalizable matrix $M=V\Lambda V^{-1}$, the eigenvector condition number is $\kappa_V(M)=\inf_V \|V\|\,\|V^{-1}\|$ over all such diagonalizations, and that the $\varepsilon$-pseudospectrum is 
$$\Lambda_\varepsilon(M)=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: \|(zI-M)^{-1}\|\ge \varepsilon^{-1}\}.$$

Address either of the following questions (taking $k=n$, say):

(a) Is there a polynomial $p$ such that with probability tending to $1$ as $n\to\infty$ (over the randomness of $b$),
$$\kappa_V(Q^*AQ)\le p(n)\,?$$

(b) Does there exist $\beta$ close to $2$ and a polynomial $q$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\operatorname{area}\bigl(\Lambda_\varepsilon(Q^*AQ)\bigr)\bigr]\le q(n)\,\varepsilon^\beta\,?$$

The problem is to be resolved even in the special case where $A$ is the $n\times n$ circulant shift matrix (the permutation matrix corresponding to the cyclic shift $i\mapsto i+1 \pmod n$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly stated as open, even in the circulant-shift special case. No web evidence of a resolution was found; recent work on pseudospectral shattering and random perturbations by Banks–Kulkarni–Mukherjee–Srivastava and others addresses related questions for Gaussian-perturbed matrices but does not resolve the Krylov-compression version.

status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on eigenvector condition number and pseudospectrum area for Gaussian-perturbed matrices, related but distinct from Krylov compressions.
status_evidence.claim: Related random-perturbation results exist but do not address Krylov compressions of arbitrary A.
